newsitem.title: JAPAN: SESC to report Nomura execs to prosecutors--paper.
newsitem.headline: SESC to report Nomura execs to prosecutors--paper.

text.p: Japan's securities watchdog plans to file a complaint against three executives of Nomura Securities Co Ltd with prosecutors, the Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Thursday.

It said the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) plans to file a complaint against two former managing directors and a third executive who is still working for the firm for allegedly funnelling about 58 million yen of Nomura money to a corporate client linked to a "sokaiya" racketeer.
The paper did not say when the legal action would take place.
Sokaiya, often linked to "yakuza" crime syndicates, typically try to extort money from firms by threatening to expose dubious business practices or to disturb shareholders' meetings.
Neither the SESC nor Nomura spokesmen were immediately available to comment on the report.
